newsitem.title: USA: FCOJ futures settle firmer, Medfly concern swatted.
newsitem.headline: FCOJ futures settle firmer, Medfly concern swatted.

text.p: FCOJ futures finished firmer in in steady dealings amid continued talk about the arrival of Mediterranean fruit flies in Florida, but the threat they pose is not strong enough to push prices higher, dealers said.

July orange juice moved higher after light buy stops were triggered around 78.00 cents per lb, hitting a high of 79.50 cents, but some speculative selling near the close pared the gains, a broker said.

Talk continued about the discovery of Mediterranean fruit flies in Hillsborough County, near Tampa in Florida. Analysts and processors said about 43 flies have been discovered in mainly residential areas, but some larvae were found fruit.

Spraying to erradicate the flies was slated to start later this week, said Lisa Backman of Florida Citrus Mutual, a growers organization. "We are quite confident they will be successful in erradicating the fly," Backman said.
July orange juice closed 0.45 cent firmer at 77.50 cents, traded 79.50 to 76.60 cents. Second-position September settled up the same at 79.55 cents, below a day's high of 81.25 cents.
"I am looking for the market to go down to 72.00 to 73.00 cents in July before going back up," the broker said.
